[NLFC.5.4] **The clock source is substituted, not switched back and forth.**
The mechanism is the runtime's (RTIM.3): live reads the host's monotonic
and UTC clocks (RTIM.3.1.2), the harness clock returns the values the harness
most recently set (RTIM.3.1.3), and selecting the mock mode puts one in place
of the other (RTIM.3.1.4).

**Going live → mock fixes both origins; it reads nothing from the host.** The
mock monotonic clock starts at 0, and the mock wall clock starts unset until
the test sets it with `ds_engine_wall_clock_set` ([NTST.3.1]). Neither depends
on when the run started, so two identical runs record identical clock values.

**The switch must come before the clock is first sampled.** Once the engine has
sampled its clock, which a pump does whether or not an input has arrived,
`ds_engine_clock_set_mode` refuses the switch to mock with `DS_ERR_STATE`: the
monotonic clock never decreases ([LTIM.2.8.2]), and the held sample is by then
past the mock origin. It is the same refusal a backward
`ds_engine_clock_set` gets ([NTST.3.1]).

**Going mock → live continues from the mock time.** The engine **must**
continue the monotonic clock from the mock clock's current value, advancing
with the host's from there, so it never decreases ([LTIM.2.8.2]). The wall
clock reads the host's again. The engine does not return to the live timeline
it left: a test that set mock time explicitly ([NLFC.5.3]) has moved the
monotonic clock off it, and there is no correspondence to return to. **Do not
build a test on switching back mid-run.**
